system.name: Study Coach
system.description: A local study coach for Microsoft certification exams, starting with AZ-104: AI instructors teach each skill and the learner practises with original, documentation-checked questions

people.name: Learner
people.description: Studies for AZ-104: takes lessons, practises questions, reads the docs and fact sheets

people.name: Content maintainer
people.description: Syncs the docs, builds fact sheets and generates the question bank from the command line (the same person as the learner)

containers.description: Home, Room (live lesson), Practice, Coverage and Docs screens in the browser; proxies /api and /agents to the server

containers.name: Coach server
containers.technology: Node.js, Hono, Flue 2.3 runtime (vite dev on 127.0.0.1:8787)
containers.description: Hosts the Coach agent (lead plus specialist subagents) behind Flue's agent router and the coach JSON API for skills, sessions, practice, answers, coverage and docs

containers.name: Content pipeline

containers.name: Conversation store

containers.name: Docs corpus and fact sheets

external_systems.name: MicrosoftDocs on GitHub

summary.overview: Study Coach is a single-user application run locally. A React web app talks to one Node server that hosts a Flue Coach agent (a lead instructor delegating to per-area specialist subagents) and a Hono JSON API over a SQLite database. A separate command-line pipeline syncs the Microsoft documentation into a local corpus, builds a fact sheet per skill and generates the question bank by running a writer agent once per question, admitting a question only after a leak check and an independent verifier agree with its key. Every model call goes to MiniMax (M3 by default; M3.1 Flash is available). Generation retries a slow or failing question once on a fallback model and logs each call's tokens and cost.
findings: Every role defaults to one provider, `minimax/MiniMax-M3` (`src/coach/models.ts:1`, fallbacks at `src/coach/models.ts:15`). Generation now retries a question that times out or ends in a model error once on a fallback model (`scripts/generate.ts:144`, default at `scripts/generate.ts:261`), but a used-up plan (usage-limit 429) still stops both generation and lessons, and lessons have no fallback at all.

The server and generation runs share `data/coach.db`; this is handled with WAL and a 5 s busy timeout (`src/coach/db.ts:86-89`). Flue's own store has no such setting, so batch runs avoid it with an in-memory store (`scripts/flue-jobs.ts:107-110`), which means generation conversations are not kept.
The scaffold `Assistant` agent is still mounted at `/agents/assistant` with a hard-coded model (`src/app.ts:14`, `src/agents/assistant.ts:8`); nothing in the web app uses it.

There is no authentication on `/api` or `/agents` (`src/app.ts:11-16`); safety rests on the dev server binding to 127.0.0.1 (`package.json:9`). There is no production build or start script, only `vite dev`.

`src/coach/instructors.ts:4` imports `seed.ts`, which imports `instructors.ts` back (`src/coach/seed.ts:2`). It works because both are used only at call time; a top-level use on either side would break module loading.

Adding an area touches several places: skills in `src/coach/seed.ts`, instructors in `src/coach/instructors.ts` and `web/src/lib/instructors.ts`, colour tokens in `web/src/styles.css` and diagram nouns in `src/coach/diagram-schema.ts`.

The lead's tools and hand-overs are gated by a read-only "learner has the floor" flag (`src/tools/coach-tools.ts:185`, `src/agents/coach.ts:68-75`). Flue renders a subagent at delegation time and throws on any state write during a render, so the check must never write. An earlier version wrote there, and every hand-over failed while the evals still passed because they checked only speaker names; the eval now fails on any failed hand-over (`src/evals/coach.eval.ts:91`).

Generation runs each question as its own `flue run` process (`scripts/flue-jobs.ts:115`), so usage is recorded from inside the agent module through Flue's `observe()` (`src/coach/usage-log.ts:52-60`) and tied to the run by `GENERATE_RUN_ID` (`scripts/generate.ts:208`); the verifier's scratch conversation would otherwise be counted separately.
recommendations: Extend the fallback model to lessons, and to a usage-limit 429, so a used-up plan does not stop lessons.
Remove the scaffold Assistant route, or stop mounting it, since nothing uses it.
Keep the server bound to localhost; add authentication before exposing it on any other interface.
Break the instructors/seed cycle by moving AREAS and SKILLS into a module that imports neither.
Derive the web instructor list and colours from the server catalog (for example via /api/skills) so a new area is data in one place.
